How we work

What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 01

    1–2 weeks

    Discover

    We map how work actually moves through the firm, from intake and acceptance to engagement terms, onboarding, delivery, deadlines and billing. We meet partners, managers and the people who chase clients, and record the professional rules that shape the design, from Bar Council and ICAI limits to PMLA duties and DPDP obligations.

    Deliverables

    • Current-state map of the client journey for each practice
    • Ranked automation opportunities with effort and risk
    • Inventory of systems, data owners and access constraints
    • Professional-rule and data-protection constraints to design around

    What we need from you

    • Time with the managing partner, practice heads and operations staff
    • Read-only access or exports from the CRM, matter register and billing system
    • Current templates, checklists and engagement letters
    • The firm's confidentiality, conflict and retention policies
  2. 02

    1–2 weeks

    Design

    We design each chosen workflow step by step: triggers, data fields, templates, message wording, decision points and the named person at every checkpoint. Client-facing wording, consent text and acceptance rules are reviewed by the firm's risk or compliance partner before anything is built.

    Deliverables

    • Workflow designs with human checkpoints marked
    • Data map covering consent, minimization, access and retention
    • Draft WhatsApp and email templates for approval
    • Acceptance criteria and test cases agreed with the firm

    What we need from you

    • Decisions on qualification, conflict and escalation rules
    • Review of consent, notice and client-message wording by the firm's compliance owner
    • Named owners for templates, knowledge sources and calendars
  3. 03

    2–6 weeks

    Build

    We configure and build in the firm's own accounts wherever possible: n8n workflows, CRM and project tool setup, secure upload stores, retrieval indexes and dashboards. Templates and knowledge sources are loaded with named owners, and every AI step logs its inputs, outputs and sources.

    Deliverables

    • Working workflows in a test environment
    • Configured templates, checklists and clause libraries
    • Permission model mirroring matter staffing and information barriers
    • Logging, alerts and error handling

    What we need from you

    • Administrator or service-account access to agreed systems
    • Approved templates, clauses and sample documents
    • A WhatsApp Business account and approved templates where messaging is used
  4. 04

    1–2 weeks

    Validate & launch

    We test on real but limited cases, including the awkward ones: duplicate clients, near-miss conflict names, wrong documents, missed dates and questions the assistant should decline. Partners review outputs before launch, and staff are trained on what the system does and what remains their decision.

    Deliverables

    • Test results against the acceptance criteria
    • Access-control and confidentiality tests
    • Staff guides and short training sessions
    • Launch checklist and rollback plan

    What we need from you

    • Partner and manager time to review test outputs
    • A pilot group of staff and willing clients
    • Go-live approval from the managing or risk partner
  5. 05

    Ongoing, reviewed monthly

    Operate & improve

    After launch we monitor runs, failures and exceptions, review a sample of AI outputs with the knowledge or risk owner, update templates and calendars when laws, forms or due dates change, and add the next workflow once the first is stable.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly operations and quality report
    • Template, calendar and knowledge source updates
    • Exception and incident log with fixes
    • Roadmap for the next automations

    What we need from you

    • A named internal owner for each workflow
    • Feedback from staff and clients
    • Notice of changes in firm policy, fees or systems

Suggested first pilot

A four-week pilot: one practice, one workflow, measured

We start with one workflow in one team where the pain is clear and the data is reachable: season document collection in a CA firm, the hearing diary for a litigation team, or onboarding and status reports for a set of agency or consulting clients. The pilot runs on real work with a small group, and the measures and the continue-or-stop decision are agreed before it starts.

  • One workflow, one practice or team, and a defined set of clients or matters
  • Integration with only the systems that workflow needs, in the firm's own accounts
  • Templates and client message wording approved by the responsible partner
  • Baseline and pilot-period measures agreed in writing
  • An end-of-pilot review with a recommendation to extend, change or stop

Governance

Safe by design, owned by your team.

  • Every workflow has a named owner in the firm and a documented human checkpoint. AI steps draft, classify and summarize; they never accept clients, give advice, file returns or send fee quotes on their own.
  • Access mirrors matter staffing and information barriers. Retrieval, reports and dashboards are tested against the permission model before launch and after every change.
  • Client data is processed only in tools the firm approves, under business terms that exclude model training, with a self-hosted model option for the most sensitive matters.
  • Client messages use opt-in and approved templates, carry no privileged or strategic content, and never ask for ID numbers or statements in chat.
  • Logs record who triggered, edited and approved each output, and are kept for the period the firm's policy and the DPDP Rules require.
  • Templates, clause libraries, compliance calendars and knowledge sources each have an owner and a review date, and are updated when laws, forms or due dates change.

Compliance notes

The obligations that shape the design.

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

DPDP Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025

Firms act as data fiduciaries for client, staff and prospect data. The Rules were notified on 13 November 2025 in phases: consent manager provisions from November 2026 and most duties, including itemized notice, security safeguards, breach intimation and erasure, from May 2027. The schedule may change, so we design for these duties now. Where PMLA, tax or company law requires longer retention, that period applies. GDPR may also apply to EU personal data.

meity.gov.in · Source ↗

Advocates: no solicitation, plus privilege and conflicts

Rule 36 in Part VI, Chapter II of the Bar Council of India Rules bars advocates from soliciting work or advertising, directly or indirectly, beyond limited website particulars, and Rule 33 bars acting for the opposite party in a matter after advising or acting in it. Section 132 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 protects advocate-client communications. We build no outreach or ads for advocates, scope knowledge tools per matter and leave conflict decisions to a lawyer.

barcouncilofindia.org · Source ↗

ICAI rules on solicitation, advertising and confidentiality

Clauses (6) and (7) of Part I of the First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 restrict solicitation and advertising, and clause (1) of Part I of the Second Schedule makes disclosing client information without consent, or other than as law requires, misconduct. ICAI's revised Code of Ethics, announced in December 2025 for application from 1 April 2026, updates its advertisement and website guidance, so promotional content is checked against the current text.

icai.org · Source ↗

PMLA duties for CAs, CSs and cost accountants in specified activities

A Finance Ministry notification of 3 May 2023 made practicing CAs, company secretaries and cost and works accountants reporting entities when they carry out specified transactions for a client, such as buying or selling immovable property, managing client money or accounts, or creating and managing companies, LLPs or trusts. They must then verify clients and beneficial owners, keep records for five years, report suspicious transactions to FIU-IND and not tip off the client.

fiuindia.gov.in · Source ↗

Advertising claims: ASCI Code and CCPA guidelines

Agencies making ads for clients work within the ASCI Code, which requires objective claims to be truthful and substantiated, and the CCPA's 2022 guidelines on misleading advertisements under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which apply to advertising agencies and endorsers as well as advertisers. Our approval loop flags claims for the client to substantiate and records who signed off; it does not decide whether a claim is lawful.

ascionline.in · Source ↗

WhatsApp Business messaging and TRAI rules

WhatsApp's Business Messaging Policy requires opt-in, honoring opt-outs, approved templates outside the 24-hour customer service window, a clear route from automation to a person, and no requests for full card, account or national ID numbers in chat. Commercial SMS in India, service messages included, use DLT-registered headers and templates under TRAI's TCCCPR, and promotional SMS and calls respect DND preferences. Our reminders go only to clients who agreed to receive them.

business.whatsapp.com · Source ↗

Questions

Frequently asked.

Can a law firm use this without breaching the Bar Council's rules on advertising?

Our legal work is internal: intake for people who approach the firm, conflict checks, engagement letters, hearing diaries, drafting and knowledge search. We do not build ads, outreach sequences, lead generation or promotional content for advocates. If a firm wants to change its website, its own lawyers should confirm the content against Rule 36 and current BCI guidance. Nothing on this page is legal advice.

Will our client documents be used to train AI models?

No. We use model providers under business or API terms that exclude training on your inputs, set retention options where providers offer them, and can run a self-hosted model through Ollama for the most sensitive matters. Retrieval is limited to documents the user is already allowed to open, and every answer cites its sources.

Does the system make professional decisions?

No. AI drafts, classifies, summarizes and routes. Lawyers decide conflicts, legal positions and filings; CAs decide tax treatment, audit judgments and what is filed; partners approve scope, fees and every document that leaves the firm. Each workflow names the person at its checkpoint.

Do you scrape court or tax portals?

No. Court cause lists, eCourts case status and the income tax, GST and MCA portals are treated as official references. Staff confirm dates and download notices from them, and our workflows take over from there. Where a portal offers an official API or alert service the firm is entitled to use, we can connect to it.

We already use Tally, Zoho, Clio or iManage. Do we need to switch?

No. We integrate with the systems you already use where they allow it, through APIs, exports or structured imports, and add tools such as n8n, Airtable or Retool only where there is a gap. Naming a product on this page does not imply a partnership.

How long before we see something working?

A focused pilot on one workflow usually takes three to six weeks including design, build and validation, depending on system access and how quickly templates and rules are approved. We agree the measures and the decision point before we start.

Can you work with firms and clients outside India?

Yes. The same workflows apply, adjusted for each jurisdiction's data protection and professional rules, such as GDPR for EU personal data or the American Bar Association's guidance on lawyers' use of generative AI in the United States. Your compliance owner confirms which obligations apply.

What does it cost?

It depends on the number of workflows, systems and users. We scope a fixed-price pilot after a discovery conversation and quote ongoing support separately, in INR or your preferred currency. Tool subscriptions and usage, such as WhatsApp conversation charges or model usage, are billed by the providers to your own accounts.
